senses.gloss: (late b. h.;to speak aloud, Assyr.) to deliver, proclaim (v.
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 9:5">Lev. R. s. 9</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 14:9">Prov. XIV, 9</cite> <he>יליץ</he>) <he>הטיפש הזה מְתַרְגֵּם חובתו בפיו וכ׳</he> that fool proclaims his guilt with his own mouth and says, am I not bound to bring a sin-offering &c.?—Esp.

senses.gloss: to explain, interpret, act as an Amora (v. אֲמוֹרָא);
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: (at public service) to translate orally (in Aramaic) what has been read from the Scriptures in the original.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 3:3:19">Y. Bicc. III, 65ᵈ</cite> top <he>תי׳ ר׳ וכ׳</he> R. Jacob … (having to act as an Amora to an ignorant teacher) interpreted (the verse <cite ref="Habakkuk 2:19">Hab. II, 19</cite>) &c.
Y. Succ. V, 55ᵇ bot. מהו מפקיעין תי׳ ר׳ … מפשילים what is mafḳiʿin? R. H. (as Amora) before R. J. explained it by the word mafshilim (v. פָּשַׁל).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 88a:3">B. Bath. 88ᵃ</cite> <he>אני וארי תִּרְגֵּימְנוּהָ</he> (prob. to be read: <he>תִּירְגַּמְ׳</he>) I and the lion in our company (a great scholar) have explained it; (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 8b">Snh. 8ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 111b">Sabb. 111ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="V00942"><he>תַּרְגִּימְנָא</he></cite>, <he>תַּרְגִּימְנָהּ</he> Chald.). Ib. 53ᵃ <he>ישר וכן תִּרְגְּמָהּ וכ׳</he> it is right, and so did Aryokh (Samuel) teach it (as Amora) in Babylonia.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 49a:11">Kidd. 49ᵃ</cite>; Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 41 <he>המְתַרְגֵּם וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="R00252"><he>צוּרָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 4:6">Meg. IV, 6</cite> <he>קטן … ומתרגם</he> a minor may read from the Law and translate; a. fr.
